state: Goal `core-time-datetime`: `Core\Time\DateTime::date`, `::dayOfYear`, `::difference`, `::toInstant`, `::timeOfDay`, `::zone`, `::weekday`, `::isLeapYear`, `::format`, `::plus`, `::minus`, `::next` and `::previous` have every feature proof, perf figure included. Four members still owe proofs: `with`, `withTime`, `startOf`, `endOf`. **A perf figure is a session's job, not the driver's**: after any edit to `time.rs` or `cldr.rs` outside its test module, run `bun nv proofs --record-perf` over all four groups before the wrap (the test module does not move the impl hash). A first `--record-perf` on a busy host can print a nonsense clock (`0.0` ns/op); re-measure with `--force --reps 9` and keep the second. The Rust tests share helpers at the end of the `time.rs` test module: `zone_view_samples()`, `datetime_view` for a view member, `datetime_formatted`, and `datetime_rebuilt(member, at, rest)` for any builder, with `datetime_stepped` (count and `Core\Unit` case index: Hour 5, Day 6, Week 7, Month 8, Year 10) and `datetime_to_weekday` (Monday 0) on top of it. Nothing is blocked.

next.title: DateTime builder proofs, in file order
next.note: one file set: `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/time.rs` (registry rows, the test module tail with `datetime_rebuilt`), `tests/conformance/core/time-datetime-builders-answer-a-new-value-in-the-same-zone.nvst` (add each member to its `// covers:` line), and new files under `docs/examples/core/Time-DateTime/`, `tests/hostile/core/Time-DateTime/`, `benches/members/core/Time-DateTime/`. The `plus` and `minus` proofs are the model. Numeric results in `.nvs` need `as int`, because `dayOfYear` returns `uint`. `with` takes an options block, so its Rust test builds seven option arguments with `Value::null()` for an omitted one (`nvs_core_time_datetime_with`'s doc says so).
